result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A supplier registered without terms gets 30 days, and terms can be changed with `updateSupplier`. The full suite passes offline (610 tests, 0 failures), including 8 in `SupplierTest`.

What changed:
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component, plus a `STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30` constant. The existing 5-argument constructor defaults to 30, so the ~50 existing call sites still compile.
- **`schema.sql`**: `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`DataStore.java`**: create and update write the column. The by-name, by-country, by-rating and by-id listings read it. I also added it to the other queries that build a `Supplier` (purchase suggestions, purchased quantity, supplier performance, spending, single-supplier categories). Without that, those would silently show 30.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: three new tests. One follows your Swedish example (45 days, renegotiated to 14, checked in every listing). One checks the 30-day default. One checks that negative days are rejected.

I did not touch `DemoScenario`, and there is no separate supplier service in the repo, so registration and renegotiation go straight through `DataStore`. Nothing is committed.
